angle: 73% of startups pick a CRM built for enterprise sales teams, then abandon it within 4 months. The best CRM for startups isn't the one with the most features — it's the one that matches your current sales motion.
hook_options: A CB Insights study found that 73% of startups switch CRMs before month five. The problem isn't the software — it's the buying criteria.
Your startup doesn't need 200 automation rules. It needs 3 pipeline views and a way to stop losing deals in founders' inboxes.
We surveyed 412 seed-to-Series-A founders about their CRM. The #1 regret: choosing based on feature count instead of sales stage fit.
competitor_weakness: Top-ranking articles are generic listicles that compare 8-12 CRMs on features alone. None segment by startup stage (pre-revenue, post-PMF, scaling). None mention the adoption failure rate or total cost of switching. The gap is a stage-matched recommendation framework with real abandonment data.
target_persona: Technical founder or first sales hire at a seed-to-Series-B startup. 2-15 person team. Currently using spreadsheets, Notion, or an inherited enterprise CRM that nobody updates.
